concepts.name: G20: Origin, Formation Context and Rationale
key_dimensions: Evolution from G7/G8 Finance Ministers' meetings to a full Leaders' Summit (1999 vs 2008 elevation)
Role of 1997-98 Asian Financial Crisis as a trigger for G20's creation at Finance Minister level
2008 Global Financial Crisis as the catalyst for elevation to Heads of State/Government Summit
Distinction: Why G20 was formed instead of expanding G7/G8 — representation vs. efficiency trade-off

concepts.name: G20 Membership Composition and Criteria
key_dimensions: Current 21 members: 19 countries + European Union + African Union (added 2023, India's Presidency)
No formal criteria for membership — selected based on economic size, population, and regional representation (trap: no treaty-based entry)
Countries that are NOT members despite large economies (e.g., Pakistan, Nigeria pre-AU inclusion) — gaps and anomalies
Overlap trap: Distinguishing G20 members from G7, BRICS, and OECD members (e.g., India is G20 but not OECD)

concepts.name: G20 Institutional Structure: Presidency and Troika System
key_dimensions: Rotating Presidency: No permanent secretariat — the host country drives the agenda (trap: no fixed headquarters)
Troika mechanism — current, previous, and incoming Presidency work together for continuity (e.g., Indonesia-India-Brazil Troika)
India's G20 Presidency (2022-23): Theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future'
How the Presidency shapes priority agenda items — risk of politicization vs. consensus-driven outcomes

concepts.name: G20 Working Architecture: Tracks and Groups
key_dimensions: Two parallel tracks: Finance Track (Finance Ministers + Central Bank Governors) and Sherpa Track (political/development issues)
Key Finance Track bodies: FMCBG, Framework Working Group, Infrastructure Working Group
Key Sherpa Track Engagement Groups: B20, C20, L20, T20, W20, Y20, S20, U20 — roles and distinctions
UPSC trap: Differentiating official working groups from engagement groups and their non-binding nature

concepts.name: G20 vs. G7 vs. G8: Comparative Analysis
key_dimensions: G7 composition (US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada + EU) vs G20 — why G7 still exists alongside G20
Russia: Suspended from G8 in 2014 (Crimea annexation) making it G7 again; Russia remains in G20 (trap: different rules)
Decision-making: G7 is more cohesive/Western-aligned; G20 is more representative but consensus is harder
Agenda overlap and complementarity: G7 as a 'pre-negotiation' forum vs G20 as broader legitimacy forum

concepts.name: G20 Decision-Making Process and Legal Status of Outcomes
key_dimensions: Consensus-based decision making — no voting mechanism, no legally binding resolutions (critical UPSC trap)
Leaders' Declaration vs. Communiqué — significance, and instances where consensus failed (e.g., 2022 Bali, 2023 New Delhi on Ukraine language)
Implementation gap: G20 commitments rely on voluntary compliance — no enforcement mechanism
Role of International Organizations (IMF, World Bank, WTO, FSB) in providing technical inputs and monitoring compliance

concepts.name: G20 and Global Financial Stability: FSB and Regulatory Reforms
key_dimensions: Financial Stability Board (FSB): Established by G20 in 2009, headquartered in Basel — monitors global financial system
Post-2008 reforms driven by G20: Basel III norms, regulation of systemically important financial institutions (SIFIs)
Too-Big-To-Fail problem: G20's approach to Global Systemically Important Banks (G-SIBs) and resolution frameworks
Crypto-asset regulation: G20's push for a coordinated global framework via FSB recommendations (recent relevance)

concepts.name: G20 and International Taxation: BEPS and Global Minimum Tax
key_dimensions: OECD/G20 BEPS (Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Project — 15 Action Plans to curb tax avoidance by MNCs
Two-Pillar Solution: Pillar One (reallocation of taxing rights) and Pillar Two (15% Global Minimum Corporate Tax)
India's position: Supported GMT but raised concerns about impact on developing country tax revenues and GIFT City
UPSC trap: BEPS is an OECD initiative endorsed by G20 — not a G20-exclusive framework; implementation via domestic laws

concepts.name: G20 and Sustainable Development / Climate Finance
key_dimensions: G20 Sustainable Finance Working Group (SFWG): Frameworks for green/sustainable finance, climate risk disclosure
Fossil fuel subsidy reform commitment (G20 pledge since 2009) vs. actual implementation gap — hypocrisy critique
New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance: G20's role in bridging developed-developing country divide
India's G20 Presidency priorities: LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), disaster risk reduction, and just energy transition

concepts.name: G20 and Global Health Governance Post-COVID
key_dimensions: Pandemic Fund (formerly Financial Intermediary Fund for Pandemic Prevention): Established under G20, hosted by World Bank
100 Days Mission: G20 commitment to develop safe and effective vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics within 100 days of pathogen identification
One Health approach: G20 endorsement linking human, animal, and environmental health
COVAX and ACT-Accelerator: G20's role in equitable vaccine distribution — gap between pledges and delivery

concepts.name: G20 and Digital Economy: Data Governance and AI
key_dimensions: Osaka Track on Data Free Flow with Trust (DFFT): Japan's 2019 initiative endorsed by G20 for cross-border data flows
G20 AI Principles (2019): Based on OECD AI Principles — first intergovernmental standards on AI (non-binding)
India's Digital Economy Working Group priorities: Digital public infrastructure (DPI), cybersecurity, digital skilling
Tension between data sovereignty (India's position) and free data flow (US/EU positions) within G20 framework

concepts.name: G20 and Infrastructure Financing: PGII vs. BRI
key_dimensions: Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII): G7/G20 alternative to China's BRI — $600 billion target by 2027
India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC): Announced at 2023 New Delhi Summit — geopolitical significance
Quality Infrastructure Investment (QII) Principles: G20 framework emphasizing transparency, sustainability, debt sustainability
UPSC trap: PGII is a G7 initiative adopted within G20 context; IMEC is a separate MoU, not a G20 decision per se

concepts.name: G20 and Debt Sustainability: Common Framework and Developing Countries
key_dimensions: G20 Common Framework for Debt Treatment (2020): For low-income countries beyond DSSI — covers Chad, Ethiopia, Zambia, Ghana
Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI): G20's COVID-era relief measure — expired December 2021
Criticism of Common Framework: Slow implementation, exclusion of middle-income countries, China's participation concerns
UPSC trap: Common Framework is for debt restructuring, NOT debt cancellation; private creditors' participation is voluntary

concepts.name: G20 India Presidency 2023: Key Outcomes and Firsts
key_dimensions: African Union's permanent membership — India's key achievement; first expansion since EU joined
New Delhi Leaders' Declaration: Consensus achieved despite geopolitical divisions on Ukraine (referred to as 'human suffering' not 'Russian aggression')
Jan Bhagidari initiative: 'People's G20' — over 200 meetings across 60 Indian cities, making it the largest G20 presidency
Key deliverables: Global Biofuels Alliance, IMEC, Green Development Pact, Deccan High Level Principles on food security

concepts.name: G20 and Food Security: Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS)
key_dimensions: AMIS: Launched by G20 in 2011 to enhance food market transparency and policy coordination — hosted by FAO
Rapid Response Forum (RRF) under AMIS: Policy coordination mechanism during food price crises
G20 Agricultural Market Working Group: Addressing price volatility, export restrictions during crises (COVID, Ukraine war)
Tension: G20 calls for open trade in agriculture vs. individual member countries imposing food export bans (India's rice export restrictions)

concepts.name: G20 and Trade: WTO Reform and Anti-Protectionism Commitments
key_dimensions: G20's standstill commitment on protectionist measures (since 2008) — vs. reality of rising tariffs and trade wars
WTO Dispute Settlement reform: G20's push to restore Appellate Body (paralyzed since 2019 due to US blocking appointments)
E-commerce moratorium: G20 members supporting continuation of WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions
UPSC trap: G20 is not a trade negotiating body — WTO is; G20 provides political impetus but cannot replace WTO negotiations

concepts.name: G20 Engagement with Non-Member Countries and International Organizations
key_dimensions: Guest/Invitee countries at G20 summits: Not permanent members — invited by Presidency (e.g., Bangladesh, UAE, Nigeria invited by India)
Permanent observer organizations: UN, IMF, World Bank, WTO, ILO, FSB, OECD, WHO attend regularly
Outreach to regional bodies: ASEAN chair, African Union (now permanent), NEPAD invited as rotating guests
UPSC trap: Guest countries have no voting rights and their attendance is at the discretion of the Presidency — no automatic inclusion

concepts.name: G20's Role in IMF Governance and Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
key_dimensions: G20's push for IMF quota reform: Increasing voting share of emerging economies (BRICS) at the cost of over-represented European nations
2021 SDR allocation of $650 billion: G20-endorsed to help COVID-recovery — largest in IMF history
Rechanneling SDRs: G20 initiative for wealthy nations to voluntarily rechannel unused SDRs to vulnerable countries via IMF's PRGT and RST
UPSC trap: SDRs are allocated by IMF, not G20 — G20 endorses and coordinates political will but cannot direct IMF technically

concepts.name: G20 and Gender Equality: Women's Economic Empowerment
key_dimensions: W20 (Women 20): Official engagement group — provides gender recommendations to G20 Leaders, not a decision-making body
Brisbane Goal (2014): G20 commitment to reduce gender gap in labour force participation by 25% by 2025 — progress and shortfalls
G20 EMPOWER: Alliance for Empowerment of Women in the Private Sector — voluntary private sector commitments
India's W20 priorities under 2023 Presidency: Women-led development, financial inclusion, digital literacy for women

concepts.name: Criticisms and Limitations of G20 as a Global Governance Body
key_dimensions: Legitimacy deficit: G20 is self-selected, non-democratic, excludes ~170 UN members — contrast with UN's universal membership
Implementation gap: No compliance mechanism — G20 tracker studies show ~70% compliance on average, varies by issue
Geopolitical paralysis: Russia-Ukraine war showed how geopolitical divisions can prevent meaningful communiqués
Overlap and coordination problems: G20 mandates overlap with IMF, WTO, UNEP, WHO — risk of fragmentation of global governance
